requirement:
`habeas coverage-check` MUST check saved execution coverage against
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions`, returning success only when
every applicable obligation is satisfied or has accepted exception evidence
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. The command MUST NOT
build the project, execute tests, collect coverage, or invoke an assessment model.
rationale:
structural: I found no structural obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.check` or in the three requirements supplied as mandatory inputs: `requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`, `requirements.test-coverage.check.functions` and `requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. None of the four has an Implements edge, and no review roots were supplied. Each clause specifies observable behavior only. For each one, an implementation built differently would produce the same results and still satisfy the text.

- **`habeas coverage-check` MUST check saved coverage and MUST NOT build, run tests, collect coverage or invoke a model.** These are behavioral constraints on what the command does. The command name is the user-facing interface, not an internal structure. Any internal layout that reads saved coverage and does nothing else conforms.
- **Threshold (`check.threshold`).** The clauses are:
  - at least 80% of instrumented lines per file;
  - exact counts rather than rounded percentages, average file percentages, or a per-function 80% target;
  - a file whose executable code is not measured requires exception evidence;
  - a file with no executable obligations is reported as such;
  - the absence of recorded lines alone does not establish that a file has no executable obligations.

  All of these describe results. The text cites the index summary, selection and freshness rules, but only as the rules to apply, with no named type or interface prescribed. An alternative that computes the same verdicts with different data structures or code organization would conform.
- **Functions (`check.functions`).** Every function needs recorded execution attributable to it, or an accepted exception. Execution attributable only to a nested function or closure does not count for the enclosing function. This is a rule about attribution outcomes. It does not prescribe an algorithm, library or type.
- **Exceptions (`check.exceptions`).** Exceptions must be attached to the specific file or function they justify, and they must not excuse another item. Changes to the inputs of the citation review invalidate them. Unassessed comments do not count. Identities must be portable and must not depend on checkout paths, run identifiers, timestamps or process identifiers. These are behavioral and semantic properties of the evidence. Delegation to the citation review is a cited behavior, not a prescribed interface. Any identity scheme that satisfies the portability properties would conform.

Evidence for these behaviors belongs to the behavioral and test criterion, not to implementation roots. No implementation root is needed here.

behavioral: **Obligations**
1. `habeas coverage-check` checks saved coverage against the file threshold (`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`) and the function rule (`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions`). It succeeds only when every applicable obligation is met or has accepted exception evidence (`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`).
2. It MUST NOT build, execute tests, collect coverage, or invoke an assessment model.

The detailed threshold, function and exception rules are the subject of those requirements' own assessments. The subject is judged here as the combined pass/fail gate plus the prohibition on side effects.

**Pass/fail gate**
- `src/execution_coverage/check.rs#mod[tests]/fn[accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution]` covers these cases:
  - A file exception does not waive a zero-execution function, so the report fails.
  - File and function exceptions together make the report pass.
  - An unmeasured function with an accepted exception passes.
  - A fully covered function passes even when a citation is present.
  - An unmeasured file with an accepted exception passes.
  - A review determination of false or `FIXME` makes the report fail.
- `src/execution_coverage/check.rs#mod[tests]/fn[missing_and_stale_explanations_fail_the_report]` covers these cases:
  - A missing review fails the report.
  - A review determination of false or `FIXME` fails the report.
  - A review of true passes.
  - Stale file, citation or outline inputs fail the report again.
- Together these cases assert both the pass and fail outcomes of the check.
- `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[full_test_flow_checks_real_function_counters_after_all_tests]` runs the real saved check with `saved_check`. It asserts "Coverage check passed" with success status for the covered code. It asserts failure and "Coverage check failed" after a nested function is left unexecuted. It also asserts that the enclosing function is not reported (`!stdout.contains("#fn[outer]: zero execution")`).

**Prohibitions**
- `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[book_rendering_preserves_retained_coverage_and_never_launches_tests]` runs standalone `habeas coverage-check` with a `cargo` shim. The shim records and rejects every subcommand except `metadata`. The test asserts these things:
  - The command still reports the "File execution coverage" output.
  - No forbidden command file exists, so there was no build or collection.
  - The test-execution marker file is absent, so no test ran.
  - The retained coverage files are byte-identical before and after.
- In the full-flow test, `saved_check` runs against a local model tripwire server. The test asserts that the request count is 0 and that the `evidence` directory is unchanged, so no assessment model is invoked.

I found no obligation without a test that exercises it and asserts its outcome. The tests carry `{test}` markers for the subject, so I found no marking gap either.

text: :::{req} check
`habeas coverage-check` MUST check saved execution coverage against
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions`, returning success only when
every applicable obligation is satisfied or has accepted exception evidence
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. The command MUST NOT
build the project, execute tests, collect coverage, or invoke an assessment model.
:::{req} check.threshold
Each first-party Rust file under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing` MUST have at least 80%
execution coverage of its instrumented lines, or current accepted exception
evidence explaining why the file falls below that target under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Counts MUST use the
file-and-line union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`;
a line counts as executed when any eligible test process or its associated
child processes has a positive execution count for it.
The check MUST use the combined selection and freshness rules of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, restricted to the active
build configuration. It MUST compare exact counts rather than rounded displayed
percentages, average file percentages, or impose an 80% target within each
function. A file whose executable code is not measured MUST require exception
evidence rather than pass with a fabricated percentage. A file established to
contain no executable coverage obligations MUST be reported as such and MUST
NOT require a threshold exception.
Absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish that a file
contains no executable coverage obligations.
:::{req} check.functions
Every function under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.scope` without
recorded execution attributable to it MUST have current accepted exception
evidence under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`, even when
its containing file meets the target of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`.
Execution attributable only to another function, including a nested function
or closure, MUST NOT establish coverage of the enclosing function merely
because their source locations overlap. Having no recorded lines alone MUST
NOT establish that a function has no executable coverage obligations.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
